title.zh: 卷十四 唐太祖家人傳第二:
title.en: Volume 14: Taizu of Later Tang's Family
title.raw: 卷十四 唐太祖家人傳第二: Volume 14: Taizu of Later Tang's Family

sentences.zh: 太祖劉太妃貞簡皇后曹氏

translations.literal: Taizu: Grand Consort Liu; Empress Zhenjian, Lady Cao
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s Grand Consort Liu and Empress Zhenjian, Lady Cao

sentences.zh: 太祖正室劉氏，代北人也；

translations.literal: Taizu’s principal wife was the Liu clan, a woman of northern Dai;
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s chief wife, Lady Liu, came from northern Dai;

sentences.zh: 其次妃曹氏，太原人也。

translations.literal: his next consort was Lady Cao of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: his secondary consort was Lady Cao of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖封晉王，劉氏封秦國夫人。

translations.literal: When Taizu was enfeoffed Prince of Jin, Liu was created Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu became Prince of Jin, Liu was titled Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 自太祖起兵代北，劉氏常從征伐。

translations.literal: From the time Taizu raised troops in northern Dai, Liu often followed on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: From Taizu’s first campaigns in northern Dai, Liu marched with him.

sentences.zh: 為人明敏多智略，頗習兵機，常教其侍妾騎射，以佐太祖。

translations.literal: Clever and resourceful, well versed in military affairs, she often taught her attendants riding and archery to assist Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Sharp-witted and versed in strategy, she trained her maids in riding and archery to aid Taizu.

sentences.zh: 太祖東追黃巢，還軍過梁，館於封禪寺。

translations.literal: Taizu pursued Huang Chao eastward; returning, his army passed through Liang and lodged at Fengchan Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Huang Chao east, Taizu marched back through Liang and quartered at Fengchan Temple.

sentences.zh: 梁王邀太祖入城，置酒上源驛，夜半以兵攻之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang invited Taizu into the city, set wine at Shangyuan Post, and at midnight attacked with troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang prince lured him into the city for wine at Shangyuan Post, then struck at midnight.

sentences.zh: 太祖左右有先脫歸者，以難告夫人，夫人神色不動，立斬告者，陰召大將謀保軍以還。

translations.literal: Some of Taizu’s men who had escaped first reported the disaster to the lady; she did not change expression, immediately executed the informants, and secretly summoned generals to plan saving the army and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Men who had broken out first brought word to the lady; she never flinched, had the messengers killed at once, and quietly rallied the generals to save the army and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 遲明，太祖還，與夫人相向慟哭，因欲舉兵擊梁。

translations.literal: At dawn Taizu returned; he and the lady faced each other and wept bitterly, and he wished to raise troops and strike Liang.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak Taizu returned; husband and wife wept together, and he meant to march against Liang.

sentences.zh: 夫人曰：「公本為國討賊，今梁事未暴，而遽反兵相攻，天下聞之，莫分曲直。

translations.literal: The lady said: “My lord originally took up arms for the state against bandits; Liang’s deed is not yet exposed, and to turn at once to mutual attack—when all under Heaven hears of it, none will know who is right.
translations.idiomatic: She said: “You took the field for the realm against rebels; Liang’s treachery is not yet public. If you turn your arms on them now, the world will not know who is in the right.

sentences.zh: 不若斂軍還鎮，自訴於朝。

translations.literal: Better to gather the army, return to your command, and appeal to the court yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Better withdraw to your post and lay the case before the court.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖從之。

translations.literal: ” Taizu followed her advice.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu took her counsel.

sentences.zh: 其後，太祖擊劉仁恭，敗歸。

translations.literal: Later Taizu attacked Liu Rengong and returned defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attacked Liu Rengong and came back beaten.

sentences.zh: 梁遣氏叔琮、康懷英等連歲攻晉，圍太原，晉兵屢敗，太祖憂窘，不知所為。

translations.literal: Liang sent Shi Shuzong, Kang Huaiying, and others to attack Jin year after year, besieging Taiyuan; Jin forces were repeatedly defeated; Taizu was distressed and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Shi Shuzong, Kang Huaiying, and others against Jin for years, besieging Taiyuan; Jin troops lost again and again, and Taizu was desperate.

sentences.zh: 大將李存信等勸太祖亡入北邊，收兵以圖再舉，太祖然之。

translations.literal: The general Li Cunxin and others urged Taizu to flee into the northern marches, gather troops, and plan another rising; Taizu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin and others urged him to flee north, regroup, and try again; Taizu agreed.

sentences.zh: 入以語夫人，夫人問誰為此謀者，曰：「存信也。

translations.literal: He told the lady; she asked who had given this counsel, and he said: “Cunxin.
translations.idiomatic: He told the lady, who asked whose plan it was. “Cunxin’s,” he said.

sentences.zh: 」夫人罵曰：「存信，代北牧羊兒耳，安足與計成敗邪！

translations.literal: ” The lady cursed: “Cunxin is a shepherd boy from northern Dai—how is he fit to decide success or failure!
translations.idiomatic: She swore: “Cunxin is a shepherd lad from the north—what does he know of victory or ruin!

sentences.zh: 且公嘗笑王行瑜棄邠州走，卒為人擒，今乃自為此乎？

translations.literal: Moreover you once mocked Wang Xingyu for abandoning Binzhou and fleeing, only to be captured in the end—will you do this yourself now?
translations.idiomatic: You laughed at Wang Xingyu for abandoning Bin and running, only to be taken—will you do the same?

sentences.zh: 昔公亡在達靼，幾不能自脫，賴天下多故，乃得南歸。

translations.literal: In the past you were exiled among the Tatars and barely escaped; you owed your return south to turmoil everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: You once lived among the Tatars and barely got away; only the chaos of the times let you come south again.

sentences.zh: 今屢敗之兵，散亡無幾，一失其守，誰肯從公？

translations.literal: Now, after repeated defeats, your scattered troops are few; lose your foothold and who will follow you?
translations.idiomatic: Your beaten troops are few; lose your base and who follows you?

sentences.zh: 北邊其可至乎？

translations.literal: Can you even reach the northern marches?
translations.idiomatic: Could you even reach the north?”

sentences.zh: 」太祖大悟而止。

translations.literal: ” Taizu was greatly enlightened and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu saw clearly and abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 已而亡兵稍稍復集。

translations.literal: Before long scattered soldiers gradually reassembled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon stragglers drifted back.

sentences.zh: 夫人無子，性賢，不妒忌，常為太祖言：「曹氏相，當生貴子，宜善待之。

translations.literal: The lady had no sons, was virtuous and free of jealousy, and often told Taizu: “Lady Cao has the look of one who will bear a noble son; you should treat her well.
translations.idiomatic: Childless but kind and without jealousy, she often said: “Lady Cao’s face promises a noble heir—treat her well.

sentences.zh: 」而曹氏亦自謙退，因相得甚歡。

translations.literal: ” Lady Cao also humbled herself, and the two were very fond of each other.
translations.idiomatic: ” Lady Cao in turn was modest, and the two women grew close.

sentences.zh: 莊宗敬皇后劉氏

translations.literal: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing, the Liu clan
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong’s Empress Jing, Lady Liu

sentences.zh: 其父聞劉氏已貴，詣魏宮上謁。

translations.literal: Her father, hearing that Liu had risen high, came to the Wei palace to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: When her father heard she had risen, he came to the Wei palace to see her.

sentences.zh: 莊宗召袁建豐問之，建豐曰：「臣始得劉氏於成安北塢，時有黃須丈人護之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong summoned Yuan Jianfeng and asked; Jianfeng said: “When I first took Lady Liu at Cheng’an’s north stockade, a yellow-bearded old man was protecting her.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong called Yuan Jianfeng, who said: “I first took Lady Liu at the north stockade of Cheng’an; a yellow-bearded elder was guarding her.

sentences.zh: 」乃出劉叟示建豐，建豐曰：「是也。

translations.literal: ” He produced Old Liu for Jianfeng; Jianfeng said: “This is he.
translations.idiomatic: ” Old Liu was brought out; Jianfeng said: “That is the man.

sentences.zh: 」然劉氏方與諸夫人爭寵，以門望相高，因大怒曰：「妾去鄉時，略可記憶，妾父不幸死於亂兵，妾時環屍慟哭而去。

translations.literal: ” But Liu was then contending with the other ladies for favor, competing in pedigree, and in great anger said: “When I left my village I can still remember: my father unluckily died among mutinous soldiers, and I wailed over his corpse and left.
translations.idiomatic: ” Liu was then fighting the other consorts for rank and flew into a rage: “I remember leaving home—my father died in the soldiers’ riot, and I wept over his body and fled.

sentences.zh: 此田舍翁安得至此！

translations.literal: How could this rustic have come here!
translations.idiomatic: How could this peasant be here!

sentences.zh: 」因命笞劉叟於宮門。

translations.literal: ” She ordered Old Liu flogged at the palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: ” She had him beaten at the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 莊宗已即皇帝位，欲立劉氏為皇后，而韓夫人正室也，伊夫人位次在劉氏上，以故難其事而未發。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had already taken the throne and wished to make Liu empress, but Lady Han was the principal wife and Lady Yi ranked above Liu, so the matter was hard and not yet carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong wished to make Liu empress, but Lady Han was principal wife and Lady Yi outranked her, so the matter stalled.

sentences.zh: 宰相豆盧革、樞密使郭崇韜希旨，上章言劉氏當立，莊宗大悅。

translations.literal: The chief minister Doulu Ge and the commissioner Guo Chongtao toed the line, memorializing that Liu should be enthroned; Zhuangzong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Chief minister Doulu Ge and commissioner Guo Chongtao flattered him with a memorial that Liu should be empress; Zhuangzong was delighted.

sentences.zh: 同光二年四月已卯，皇帝御文明殿，遣使冊劉氏為皇后。

translations.literal: On jimao, the fourth month of the second year of Tongguang, the emperor held court at the Hall of Civil Splendor and sent envoys to invest Liu as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the fourth month of Tongguang 2, he held court at the Hall of Civil Splendor and invested Liu as empress.

sentences.zh: 皇后受冊，乘重翟車，鹵簿、鼓吹，見於太廟。

translations.literal: The empress received the patent, rode the heavy pheasant carriage, with guards and music, and appeared at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: She took the patent in the state carriage, with guards and music, and was presented at the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 韓夫人等皆不平之，乃封韓氏為淑妃，伊氏為德妃。

translations.literal: Lady Han and the others were all resentful; Han was then created Shufei and Yi Defei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Han and the others seethed; Han was made Shufei and Yi Defei.

sentences.zh: 莊宗自滅梁，誌意驕怠，宦官、伶人亂政，后特用事於中。

translations.literal: After Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, his will grew proud and slack; eunuchs and actors threw government into chaos, and the empress especially wielded power within.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang fell, Zhuangzong grew arrogant and lax; eunuchs and actors ruined government, and the empress ruled from within.

sentences.zh: 自以出於賤微，逾次得立，以為佛力。

translations.literal: She thought that, rising from the lowest ranks and leapfrogging to the throne, it was the Buddha’s doing.
translations.idiomatic: She believed her leap from humble birth to the throne was Buddha’s work.

sentences.zh: 又好聚斂，分遣人為商賈，至於市肆之間，薪芻果茹，皆稱中宮所賣。

translations.literal: She also loved to amass wealth, sending people out as merchants; in the markets even firewood, fodder, fruit, and vegetables were said to be sold by the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: She hoarded wealth, sending agents to trade; in the markets even fuel, fodder, and produce were sold as “from the inner palace.”

sentences.zh: 四方貢獻，必分為二，一以上天子，一以入中宮，宮中貨賄山積。

translations.literal: Tribute from the four quarters was always split in two—one part for the Son of Heaven, one for the inner palace—and palace bribes piled like mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Every gift from the provinces was halved—half for the emperor, half for her—and the palace stores overflowed.

sentences.zh: 惟寫佛書，饋賂僧尼，而莊宗由此亦佞佛。

translations.literal: She only copied sutras and bribed monks and nuns, and Zhuangzong from this also came to dote on Buddhism.
translations.idiomatic: She copied sutras and lavished gifts on clergy, and Zhuangzong turned devout as well.

sentences.zh: 有胡僧自于闐來，莊宗率皇后及諸子迎拜之。

translations.literal: A barbarian monk came from Khotan; Zhuangzong led the empress and his sons to welcome and bow to him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk from Khotan arrived; Zhuangzong led the empress and princes out to bow.

sentences.zh: 僧遊五臺山，遣中使供頓，所至傾動城邑。

translations.literal: When the monk toured Mount Wutai, palace envoys supplied his needs; wherever he went cities were shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When he toured Wutai, imperial envoys fed his train and every town trembled.

sentences.zh: 又有僧誠惠，自言能降龍。

translations.literal: There was also the monk Chenghui, who claimed he could tame dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Another monk, Chenghui, claimed he could subdue dragons.

sentences.zh: 嘗過鎮州，王镕不為之禮，誠惠怒曰：「吾有毒龍五百，當遣一龍揭片石，常山之人，皆魚鱉也。

translations.literal: Passing through Zhenzhou, Wang Rong did not treat him with ceremony; Chenghui raged: “I have five hundred poison dragons; I will send one to lift a stone slab—the people of Changshan will all be fish and turtles.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzhou, Wang Rong slighted him; Chenghui raged: “I command five hundred poison dragons; one can lift a stone slab and drown every soul in Changshan.

sentences.zh: 」會明年滹沱河大水，壞鎮州關城，人皆以為神。

translations.literal: ” The next year the Hutuo flooded, wrecking Zhenzhou’s pass walls, and people took it for a miracle.
translations.idiomatic: ” Next year the Hutuo flooded and broke Zhenzhou’s gate; people called it divine.

sentences.zh: 莊宗及后率諸子、諸妃拜之，誠惠端坐不起，由是士無貴賤皆拜之，獨郭崇韜不拜也。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong and the empress led princes and consorts to bow; Chenghui sat upright and did not rise, so thereafter gentlemen high and low all bowed—only Guo Chongtao did not.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and the empress led the court to bow; Chenghui never rose, and soon everyone bowed—only Guo Chongtao refused.

sentences.zh: 是時，皇太后及皇后交通藩鎮，太后稱「誥令」，皇后稱「教命」，兩宮使者旁午於道。

translations.literal: At that time the empress dowager and empress trafficked with military governors; the dowager issued “edicts,” the empress “commands,” and messengers from the two palaces crowded the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Dowager and empress dealt with governors; the dowager issued “edicts,” the empress “commands,” and their envoys clogged the roads.

sentences.zh: 許州節度使溫韜以后佞佛，因請以私第為佛寺，為后薦福。

translations.literal: The military governor of Xuzhou, Wen Tao, because the empress was devoted to Buddhism, asked to make his private residence a monastery to bless her.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tao of Xuzhou, courting her piety, offered his mansion as a temple for her merit.

sentences.zh: 莊宗數幸郭崇韜、元行欽等私第，常與后俱。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong often visited the private homes of Guo Chongtao, Yuan Xingqin, and others, usually with the empress.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong often visited Guo Chongtao, Yuan Xingqin, and others, the empress always at his side.

sentences.zh: 其後幸張全義第，酒酣，命后拜全義為養父。

translations.literal: Later, visiting Zhang Quanyi’s house, when wine was deep he ordered the empress to bow to Quanyi as foster father.
translations.idiomatic: Later, drunk at Zhang Quanyi’s house, he made the empress bow to Quanyi as foster father.

sentences.zh: 全義日遣姬妾出入中宮，問遺不絕。

translations.literal: Quanyi daily sent concubines in and out of the inner palace, gifts never ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: Quanyi sent concubines to the palace daily, gifts flowing without end.

sentences.zh: 莊宗有愛姬，甚有色而生子，后心患之。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong had a favorite concubine, very beautiful, who bore a son; the empress resented it.
translations.idiomatic: A favorite concubine, lovely and with a son, drew the empress’s envy.

sentences.zh: 莊宗燕居宮中，元行欽侍側，莊宗問曰：「爾新喪婦，其復娶乎？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was at leisure in the palace; Yuan Xingqin attended; Zhuangzong asked: “You have newly lost your wife—will you marry again? I will help with the bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: At ease in the palace with Yuan Xingqin beside him, Zhuangzong asked: “Your wife has just died—will you wed again? I will pay the bride-price.

sentences.zh: 吾助爾聘。

translations.literal: I will help you betroth.
translations.idiomatic: I will arrange the match.”

sentences.zh: 」后指愛姬請曰：「帝憐行欽，何不賜之？

translations.literal: ” The empress pointed at the favorite and said: “The emperor pities Xingqin—why not give her to him?
translations.idiomatic: ” The empress pointed at the favorite: “You pity Xingqin—why not give her to him?

sentences.zh: 」莊宗不得已，陽諾之。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong had no choice and pretended to agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong had no choice and feigned assent.

sentences.zh: 后趣行欽拜謝，行欽再拜，起顧愛姬，肩輿已出宮矣。

translations.literal: The empress urged Xingqin to bow thanks; he bowed twice, rose and looked for the favorite—a sedan had already borne her from the palace.
translations.idiomatic: She hurried Xingqin to bow; he rose and looked for the girl—her litter was already gone from the palace.

sentences.zh: 莊宗不樂，稱疾不食者累日。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was unhappy and for many days claimed illness and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong sulked and for days refused food, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 同光三年秋大水，兩河之民，流徙道路，京師賦調不充，六軍之士，往往殍踣，乃預借明年夏、秋租稅，百姓愁苦，號泣於路，莊宗方與后荒於畋遊。

translations.literal: In autumn of the third year of Tongguang great floods struck; people of the two He provinces wandered the roads; the capital’s levies fell short; soldiers of the Six Armies often collapsed dead; they advanced next year’s summer and autumn taxes; the people wailed on the roads while Zhuangzong and the empress still roved in the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Tongguang 3 floods ravaged the Yellow River country; refugees clogged the roads, taxes failed, soldiers starved, and next year’s rent was collected early while Zhuangzong and the empress still hunted.

sentences.zh: 十二月己卯臘，畋於白沙，后率皇子、後宮畢從，歷伊闕，宿龕澗，癸未乃還。

translations.literal: On jimao, the twelfth month, the La festival hunt at Baisha; the empress led princes and the entire rear palace; they passed Yique, lodged at Longjian, and returned on guiwei.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao in the twelfth month they hunted at Baisha; the empress led princes and the whole harem through Yique to Longjian, returning on guiwei.

sentences.zh: 是時大雪，軍士寒凍，金槍衛兵萬騎，所至責民供給，壞什器，徹廬舍而焚之，縣吏畏懼，亡竄山谷。

translations.literal: Snow fell heavily; soldiers froze; ten thousand Golden Spear guards wherever they went forced the people to supply them, smashed utensils, tore down houses and burned them; county clerks fled into the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Snow buried the land; ten thousand guards extorted supplies, smashed goods, burned homes, and clerks fled to the hills.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，客星犯天庫，有星流於天棓。

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year a guest star violated the Celestial Treasury; a star streamed toward the Celestial Flail.
translations.idiomatic: Next third month a guest star struck the Treasury; another streaked toward the Flail.

sentences.zh: 占星者言：「御前當有急兵，宜散積聚以禳之。

translations.literal: Astrologers said: “Urgent troops will come before the throne; you should scatter hoarded goods to avert it.
translations.idiomatic: Astrologers said: “Soldiers will threaten the throne—scatter the hoards to avert disaster.

sentences.zh: 」宰相請出庫物以給軍，莊宗許之，后不肯，曰：「吾夫婦得天下，雖因武功，蓋亦有天命。

translations.literal: ” The chief ministers asked to take treasury goods for the army; Zhuangzong agreed; the empress refused, saying: “We husband and wife won the realm—though by arms, surely there was Heaven’s mandate too.
translations.idiomatic: ” Ministers asked to open the stores for the troops; Zhuangzong agreed; she refused: “We won the realm by the sword, but Heaven ordained it too.

sentences.zh: 命既在天，人如我何！

translations.literal: Once fate is in Heaven, what can men do to us!
translations.idiomatic: Fate rests with Heaven—what can men do?”

sentences.zh: 」宰相論於延英，后於屏間耳屬之，因取妝奩及皇幼子滿喜置帝前曰：「諸侯所貢，給賜已盡，宮中所有惟此耳，請鬻以給軍！

translations.literal: ” The ministers argued in Yanying; the empress listened from behind the screen and took her jewel box and the infant prince Manxi before the emperor, saying: “What the lords gave is spent in gifts; all the palace has is this—sell it for the army!
translations.idiomatic: ” In council she listened behind the screen, then set her jewel box and the child Manxi before him: “The lords’ gifts are gone; this is all we have—sell it for the troops!

sentences.zh: 」宰相惶恐而退。

translations.literal: ” The ministers withdrew in fear.
translations.idiomatic: ” The ministers fled in dismay.

sentences.zh: 及趙在禮作亂，出兵討魏，始出物以賫軍，軍士負而詬曰：「吾妻子已饑死，得此何為！」

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled and troops went to punish Wei, goods were at last issued to reward the army; soldiers shouldered them and cursed: “Our wives and children have starved—what use is this!”
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rose and the army marched on Wei, pay was issued at last; soldiers cursed: “Our families are dead—what is this to us!”

sentences.zh: 莊宗東幸汴州，從駕兵二萬五千，及至萬勝，不得進而還，軍士離散，所亡太半。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong went east to Bianzhou with twenty-five thousand escorts; reaching Wansheng he could not advance and turned back; soldiers scattered and more than half were lost.
translations.idiomatic: He went east to Bian with twenty-five thousand men; blocked at Wansheng, he turned back and lost more than half his force.

sentences.zh: 至罌子谷，道路隘狹，莊宗見從官執兵仗者，皆以好言勞之曰：「適報魏王平蜀，得蜀金銀五十萬，當悉給爾等。

translations.literal: At Yingzi Valley the road was narrow; Zhuangzong saw followers with weapons and spoke kindly: “We have just heard the Prince of Wei pacified Shu and gained five hundred thousand in gold and silver—we will give it all to you.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzi Valley he spoke to armed followers: “Word came that the Prince of Wei took Shu and five hundred thousand in gold and silver—it is all for you.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下與之太晚，得者亦不感恩。

translations.literal: ” They answered: “Your Majesty gave too late; those who get it will not be grateful.
translations.idiomatic: ” They answered: “Too late, sire—even those who receive it will not thank you.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗泣下，因顧內庫使張容哥索袍帶以賜之，容哥對曰：「盡矣。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong wept, turned to the inner treasury commissioner Zhang Rongge for robes and belts to give; Rongge answered: “Gone.
translations.idiomatic: ” He wept and asked Zhang Rongge for robes and belts; Rongge said: “Nothing left.

sentences.zh: 」軍士叱容哥曰：「致吾君至此，皆由爾輩！

translations.literal: ” The soldiers shouted at Rongge: “You brought our lord to this—it is all your doing!
translations.idiomatic: ” Soldiers shouted: “You brought our lord to this—all of you!

sentences.zh: 」因抽刀逐之，左右救之而免。

translations.literal: ” They drew swords and chased him; attendants saved him.
translations.idiomatic: ” They drew swords; attendants barely saved him.

sentences.zh: 容哥曰：「皇后惜物，不以給軍，而歸罪於我。

translations.literal: Rongge said: “The empress hoarded goods and would not give them to the army, yet the blame falls on me.
translations.idiomatic: Rongge said: “The empress would not pay the army, yet I am blamed.

sentences.zh: 事若不測，吾身萬段矣！

translations.literal: If things go wrong, my body will be cut in ten thousand pieces!
translations.idiomatic: If disaster comes, I will be torn limb from limb!

sentences.zh: 」乃投水而死。

translations.literal: ” He threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: ” He drowned himself.

sentences.zh: 郭從謙反，莊宗中流矢，傷甚，臥絳霄殿廓下，渴欲得飲，后令宦官進飧酪，不自省視。

translations.literal: Guo Congqian rebelled; Zhuangzong was struck by an arrow, badly wounded, lying under the colonnade of Jiangxiao Hall, thirsty and wanting drink; the empress ordered eunuchs to bring broth and cheese and did not look in on him herself.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Congqian rebelled, Zhuangzong took an arrow and lay under Jiangxiao Hall, parched; the empress sent broth and cheese by eunuch and never came to him.

sentences.zh: 莊宗崩，后與李存渥等焚嘉慶殿，擁百騎出師子門。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong died, the empress with Li Cunwo and others burned Jiaqing Hall and led a hundred horsemen out Shizi Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At his death she burned Jiaqing Hall with Li Cunwo and fled Shizi Gate with a hundred riders.

sentences.zh: 后於馬上以囊盛金器寶帶，欲於太原造寺為尼。

translations.literal: On horseback she packed gold vessels and jeweled belts in bags, intending to build a temple at Taiyuan and become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: On horseback she stuffed gold and jeweled belts into sacks, planning a nunnery at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 在道與存渥奸，及至太原，乃削髮為尼。

translations.literal: On the road she lay with Cunwo; reaching Taiyuan, she shaved her head and became a nun.
translations.idiomatic: On the road she took Cunwo as lover; at Taiyuan she shaved her head.

sentences.zh: 明宗入立，遣人賜后死。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he sent men to grant her death.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent men to grant her death.

sentences.zh: 晉天福五年，追謚曰神閔敬皇后。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfu of Jin she was posthumously titled Empress Shenmin Jing.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Tianfu 5 she was posthumously titled Empress Shenmin Jing.

sentences.zh: 自唐末喪亂，后妃之制不備，至莊宗時，後宮之數尤多，有昭容、昭儀、昭媛、出使、禦正、侍真、懿才、咸一、瑤芳、懿德、宣一等，其餘名號，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Since the chaos at the end of Tang the system for empresses and consorts was incomplete; under Zhuangzong the rear palace was especially numerous—Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, Zhaoyuan, Chushi, Yuzheng, Shizhen, Yicai, Xianyi, Yaofang, Yide, Xuanyi, and others; the rest of the titles cannot be counted.
translations.idiomatic: After Tang’s fall the harem rites were broken; under Zhuangzong titles multiplied beyond count—Zhaorong, Zhaoyi, Zhaoyuan, and dozens more.

sentences.zh: 莊宗遇弒，後宮散走，朱守殷入宮，選得三十餘人。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was assassinated the rear palace scattered; Zhu Shouyin entered the palace and took more than thirty women.
translations.idiomatic: At the assassination the harem fled; Zhu Shouyin took thirty-odd women.

sentences.zh: 虢國夫人夏氏以嘗幸於莊宗，守殷不敢留。

translations.literal: Lady Xia of Guo, once favored by Zhuangzong, Shouyin did not dare keep.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia of Guo, whom Zhuangzong had favored, Shouyin dared not keep.

sentences.zh: 明宗立，悉放莊宗時宮人還其家，獨夏氏無所歸，乃以河陽節度使夏魯奇同姓也，因以歸之，後嫁契丹突欲李贊華。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he released all Zhuangzong’s palace women to their homes; only Lady Xia had nowhere to go; as the military governor of Heyang, Xia Luqi, shared the surname, she was given to his household, and later married the Khitan prince Tuyu Li Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong sent Zhuangzong’s women home; only Lady Xia remained and was given to Xia Luqi of Heyang for the shared surname, then married the Khitan prince Li Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 贊華性酷毒，喜殺人，婢妾微過，常加刲灼。

translations.literal: Zanhua was cruel and loved killing; for slight faults maids were often branded and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Zanhua was vicious, branding and burning maids for trifles.

sentences.zh: 夏氏懼，求離婚，及削髮為尼以卒。

translations.literal: Lady Xia feared, sought divorce, shaved her head as a nun, and died.
translations.idiomatic: She feared him, sought divorce, took the tonsure, and died.

sentences.zh: 而韓淑妃、伊德妃皆居太原，晉高祖反時，為契丹所虜。

translations.literal: Lady Han the Shufei and Lady Yi the Defei both lived at Taiyuan; when Gaozu of Jin rebelled they were captured by the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Shufei Han and Defei Yi lived at Taiyuan and were taken by the Khitan when Jin Gaozu rose.

sentences.zh: 太祖四弟

translations.literal: Taizu’s four younger brothers
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s four younger brothers

sentences.zh: 唐自朱邪得姓而為李氏，得國而為晉，得天下而為唐。

translations.literal: Tang: from the Zhuye they took the surname Li, gained a state and became Jin, gained the realm and became Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang began as the Zhuye who took the name Li, became Jin, then Tang.

sentences.zh: 其始出於夷狄，而終以亂亡，故其世次不可詳見。

translations.literal: They began among the barbarians and ended in chaotic ruin, so their generations cannot be seen in full.
translations.idiomatic: They rose from the borderlands and fell in chaos, so their line cannot be traced fully.

sentences.zh: 其可見者，曰太祖四弟、八子、五孫，三世而絕。

translations.literal: What can be seen: Taizu’s four brothers, eight sons, five grandsons—three generations then extinct.
translations.idiomatic: What survives in the record: four brothers, eight sons, five grandsons—three generations, then nothing.

sentences.zh: 太祖四弟，曰克讓、克修、克恭、克寧，皆不知其父母名號。

translations.literal: Taizu’s four brothers: Kerang, Kexiu, Kegong, and Kening—the names of their parents are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The four were Kerang, Kexiu, Kegong, and Kening; their parents’ names are lost.

sentences.zh: 克讓，少善騎射，為振武軍校，從討王仙芝，以功拜金吾衛將軍，留京師。

translations.literal: Kerang in youth excelled at riding and archery, was an officer of Zhenwu Army, followed the campaign against Wang Xianzhi, and by merit was made general of the Golden Guard, remaining in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang excelled at horsemanship and archery, served in Zhenwu, campaigned against Wang Xianzhi, and won a post in the Golden Guard at court.

sentences.zh: 李氏自憲宗時以部族歸唐，唐處之河西，嘗遣一子宿衛京師，賜第於親仁坊。

translations.literal: The Li clan since Emperor Xianzong had submitted their tribe to Tang; Tang settled them west of the river and once sent a son to guard the capital, granting a mansion in Qinren Ward.
translations.idiomatic: Since Xianzong the Li had submitted; Tang settled them west of the river and kept a son at court in a mansion on Qinren Lane.

sentences.zh: 其後太祖起兵雲中，殺唐守將段文楚。

translations.literal: Later Taizu raised troops in Yunzhong and killed the Tang garrison commander Duan Wenchu.
translations.idiomatic: Later Taizu rose in Yunzhong and killed the Tang commander Duan Wenchu.

sentences.zh: 唐發兵討太祖，遣王處存以兵圍親仁坊，捕宿衛子克讓。

translations.literal: Tang sent troops against Taizu and dispatched Wang Chucun to surround Qinren Ward and seize the hostage son Kerang.
translations.idiomatic: Tang marched on him; Wang Chucun besieged Qinren Ward to seize Kerang.

sentences.zh: 克讓與其仆何相溫、石的歷等十餘騎，彎弧躍馬，突圍而出。

translations.literal: Kerang with his servant He Xiangwen, Shi Deli, and a dozen riders bent bows, leaped horses, and broke out.
translations.idiomatic: Kerang with He Xiangwen, Shi Deli, and a dozen men shot their way out.

sentences.zh: 處存以千餘人追至渭橋，克讓等射殺百餘人，追兵乃止，克讓奔於雁門。

translations.literal: Chucun with over a thousand pursued to Wei Bridge; Kerang and the others shot down more than a hundred and the pursuit stopped; Kerang fled to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Chucun pursued with a thousand to Wei Bridge; they killed a hundred and escaped to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 明年，太祖復歸唐，克讓還宿衛京師。

translations.literal: The next year Taizu returned to Tang allegiance and Kerang resumed guard duty in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Taizu submitted again and Kerang returned to court.

sentences.zh: 黃巢犯長安，克讓守潼關，為賊所敗，奔於南山，匿佛寺，為寺僧所殺。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao struck Chang’an, Kerang held Tong Pass, was defeated by the rebels, fled to the southern hills, hid in a monastery, and was killed by the monks.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao took Chang’an, Kerang held Tong Pass, was beaten, hid in a monastery in the southern hills, and monks killed him.

sentences.zh: 克修字崇遠，從討龐勛，以功拜朔州刺史。

translations.literal: Kexiu, style Chongyuan, followed the campaign against Pang Xun and by merit was made prefect of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kexiu, styled Chongyuan, fought Pang Xun and became prefect of Shuo.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮雁門，以為奉誠軍使。

translations.literal: When Taizu held Yanmen, he was made commissioner of Fengcheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu held Yanmen, he was made commissioner of Fengcheng.

sentences.zh: 從入關，討黃巢，為先鋒，遷左營軍使。

translations.literal: Following into the passes to attack Huang Chao, he was vanguard and was promoted to commissioner of the Left Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the passes against Huang Chao as vanguard and became commissioner of the Left Camp.

sentences.zh: 潞州孟方立遷於邢州，晉取潞州，表克修昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Meng Fangli of Luzhou moved to Xingzhou; Jin took Luzhou and memorialized Kexiu as military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Fangli left Luzhou for Xing, Jin took it and made Kexiu governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 數出山東擊方立，又與李罕之攻寇懷、孟之間。

translations.literal: He repeatedly came out to Shandong to strike Fangli and with Li Hanzhi raided between Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Shandong against Fangli and with Li Hanzhi harried Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 其後，太祖自將擊方立，還軍過潞，克修性儉嗇，供饋甚薄，太祖大怒，詬而擊笞之。

translations.literal: Later Taizu himself attacked Fangli; returning through Lu, Kexiu was frugal and stingy and his supplies were very thin; Taizu raged, reviled him, and beat him with a staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu passed through Lu after attacking Fangli, Kexiu’s meager hospitality enraged him; he cursed and beat him with a staff.

sentences.zh: 克修慚憤，發疾卒。

translations.literal: Kexiu died of shame and anger in a sudden illness.
translations.idiomatic: Kexiu died of shame and rage.

sentences.zh: 二子：嗣弼、嗣肱。

translations.literal: Two sons: Sibi and Sigu.
translations.idiomatic: He left two sons: Sibi and Sigu.

sentences.zh: 嗣弼為涿州刺史，天祐十九年，契丹攻破涿州，嗣弼歿於虜。

translations.literal: Sibi was prefect of Zhuo; in the nineteenth year of Tianyou the Khitan took Zhuo and Sibi perished among the captives.
translations.idiomatic: Sibi governed Zhuo; in Tianyou 19 the Khitan took the city and he died captive.

sentences.zh: 嗣肱少有膽略，從周德威數立戰功，為馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Sigu in youth had daring and strategy; following Zhou Dewei he won many battles and was made chief adjutant of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Sigu was bold; under Zhou Dewei he won many fights and became chief adjutant of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 李存審敗梁軍於胡壁，嗣肱獲梁將一人。

translations.literal: When Li Cunshen defeated Liang at Hubi, Sigu captured a Liang general.
translations.idiomatic: At Hubi, with Li Cunshen’s victory, Sigu took a Liang general.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖圍蓚縣，嗣肱從存審救蓚，梁軍解去，嗣肱功為多，超拜蔚州刺史、雁門以北都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: When Liang’s Taizu besieged Zhuo, Sigu followed Cunshen to relieve it; the Liang army withdrew; Sigu’s merit was greatest; he was promoted to prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang besieged Zhuo, Sigu relieved it with Cunshen; his merit was greatest and he became prefect of Wei and commander north of Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 累遷澤、代二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to prefect of Ze and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He later governed Ze and Dai.

sentences.zh: 新州王郁叛晉，亡入契丹，山後諸州皆叛，嗣肱取媯、儒、武三州，拜新州刺史、山北都團練使。

translations.literal: Wang Yu of Xinzhou rebelled against Jin and fled to the Khitan; the mountain posts all rebelled; Sigu took Ji, Ru, and Wu and was made prefect of Xin and regimental commissioner of the northern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu of Xin rebelled to the Khitan; Sigu recovered Ji, Ru, and Wu and became prefect of Xin and commissioner of the northern mountains.

sentences.zh: 同光元年春，卒於官。

translations.literal: In spring of the first year of Tongguang he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in spring of Tongguang 1.

sentences.zh: 克恭，初為決勝軍使。

translations.literal: Kegong at first was commissioner of Juesheng Army.
translations.idiomatic: Kegong first commanded Juesheng Army.

sentences.zh: 克修卒，以克恭代為昭義軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Kexiu died, Kegong replaced him as military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: When Kexiu died, Kegong succeeded him at Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 克修為人簡儉，潞人素安其政，且哀其見笞以死。

translations.literal: Kexiu had been simple and frugal; the people of Lu had long been at ease under his rule and pitied him for being beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kexiu had ruled Lu frugally and kindly; the people mourned his beating to death.

sentences.zh: 克恭橫暴不法，又不習軍事，由是潞人皆怨。

translations.literal: Kegong was violent and lawless and did not know military affairs, so the people of Lu all resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Kegong was brutal and ignorant of war, and Lu turned against him.

sentences.zh: 克恭選後院勁兵五百人，獻於太祖，行至銅鞮，其將馮霸以其徒叛。

translations.literal: Kegong selected five hundred stalwart rear-guard troops and presented them to Taizu; reaching Tongdi, the officer Feng Ba led his men in mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: He sent five hundred picked troops to Taizu; at Tongdi Feng Ba mutinied.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣李元審討之，戰於沁水，元審大敗被傷，奔入潞州。

translations.literal: Taizu sent Li Yuanshen to punish them; they fought at Qinshui; Yuanshen was badly defeated and wounded and fled into Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanshen was sent against them, beaten at Qinshui, and fled wounded into Lu.

sentences.zh: 牙將安居受亦叛，殺克恭及元審，使人召霸，霸不受命，居受懼而出奔，行至長子，為野人所殺，傳首於霸。

translations.literal: The牙 officer An Jushou also rebelled, killed Kegong and Yuanshen, sent men to summon Ba; Ba would not obey; Jushou fled in fear; reaching Changzi he was killed by rustics and his head sent to Ba.
translations.idiomatic: An Jushou rebelled, killed Kegong and Yuanshen, and summoned Ba, who refused; Jushou fled and rustics killed him at Changzi and sent his head to Ba.

sentences.zh: 霸乃入潞州，自稱留後，以附於梁。

translations.literal: Ba then entered Luzhou, declared himself acting governor, and submitted to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Ba entered Lu, made himself acting governor, and submitted to Liang.

sentences.zh: 克寧，為人仁孝，居諸兄弟中最賢，事太祖小心不懈。

translations.literal: Kening was humane and filial; among the brothers he was most worthy and served Taizu with unwearying care.
translations.idiomatic: Kening was kind and filial, the best of the brothers, and served Taizu tirelessly.

sentences.zh: 太祖與赫連鐸、李可舉戰雲、蔚間，後奔達靼，入破黃巢，克寧未嘗不從行。

translations.literal: When Taizu fought Helian Duo and Li Keyong between Yun and Wei, later fled to the Tatars, entered to break Huang Chao, Kening never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: From the wars with Helian Duo and Li Keyong through exile among the Tatars and the campaign against Huang Chao, Kening always marched with him.

sentences.zh: 太祖鎮太原，以為內外制置蕃漢都知兵馬使，檢校太保、振武軍節度使，軍中之事，無大小皆決克寧。

translations.literal: When Taizu held Taiyuan he was made overseer of internal and external arrangements for Han and barbarian troops, acting Grand Guardian and military governor of Zhenwu; in military affairs great and small Kening decided all.
translations.idiomatic: At Taiyuan he oversaw Han and barbarian troops as acting Grand Guardian and governor of Zhenwu; every military matter passed through him.

sentences.zh: 太祖病，召莊宗侍側，屬張承業與克寧曰：「以亞子屬公等。

translations.literal: When Taizu fell ill he summoned Zhuangzong to his side and entrusted Zhang Chengye and Kening, saying: “I leave Yazi to you.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Taizu called Zhuangzong and told Zhang Chengye and Kening: “I leave Yazi to you.

sentences.zh: 」太祖崩，莊宗告於克寧曰：「兒年孤稚，未通庶政，雖有先王之命，恐不足以當大事。

translations.literal: ” When Taizu died Zhuangzong told Kening: “I am young and ignorant of affairs; though there was the late king’s command, I fear I am not equal to great matters.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhuangzong told Kening: “I am young and untried; though Father commanded it, I fear I cannot bear the burden.

sentences.zh: 叔父勛德俱高，先王嘗任以政矣，敢以軍府煩季父，以待兒之有立。

translations.literal: Uncle’s merit and virtue are both high; the late king once entrusted you with government—I dare trouble my younger uncle with the army and government until I can stand on my own.
translations.idiomatic: Your merit is great and Father once gave you the realm—I beg you take the command until I can stand alone.

sentences.zh: 」克寧曰：「吾兄之命，以兒屬我，誰敢易之！

translations.literal: Kening said: “My elder brother’s command entrusted the boy to me—who would change it!
translations.idiomatic: Kening said: “My brother gave him to me—who would change that?

sentences.zh: 」因下而北面再拜稱賀，莊宗乃即晉王位。

translations.literal: ” He descended and bowed northward twice in congratulation, and Zhuangzong then took the throne as Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: ” He bowed north in congratulation, and Zhuangzong became Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 初，太祖起於雲、朔之間，所得驍勇之士，多養以為子，而與英豪戰爭，卒就霸業，諸養子之功為多，故尤寵愛之，衣服禮秩如嫡。

translations.literal: At first, when Taizu rose between Yun and Shuo, the fierce warriors he gained he often adopted as sons; contending with heroes in war, at last he achieved hegemony—the merit of the adopted sons was great, so he especially favored them; clothes and ritual rank were like those of legitimate sons.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu adopted many fierce warriors as sons; their merit built his power, and he favored them like true heirs in dress and rank.

sentences.zh: 諸養子麾下皆有精兵，恃功自恣，自先王時常見優假。

translations.literal: Each adopted son’s command had crack troops; relying on merit they were self-willed; even under the late king they were often indulged.
translations.idiomatic: Each led elite troops, proud of merit; even the late king indulged them.

sentences.zh: 及新王立，年少，或托疾不朝，或見而不拜。

translations.literal: When the new king was young, some feigned illness and did not attend court, or came and did not bow.
translations.idiomatic: The young king found some feigning illness, others attending without a bow.

sentences.zh: 養子存顥、存實告克寧曰：「兄亡弟及，古之道也。

translations.literal: The adopted sons Cunhao and Cunshi told Kening: “When the elder brother dies the younger succeeds—this is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Cunhao and Cunshi told Kening: “Elder brother dies, younger succeeds—that is the old law.

sentences.zh: 以叔拜侄，理豈安乎？

translations.literal: For an uncle to bow to a nephew—how can reason be at ease?
translations.idiomatic: How can an uncle bow to a nephew?

sentences.zh: 人生富貴，當自取之。

translations.literal: Life’s wealth and honor should be taken by oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune must be seized for oneself.

sentences.zh: 」克寧曰：「吾家三世，父慈子孝，先王土宇，茍有所歸，吾復何求也！」

translations.literal: Kening said: “Our house for three generations—father kind, sons filial; the late king’s domain, if it has someone to receive it, what more do I seek!”
translations.idiomatic: Kening said: “Three generations of kindness—if the realm has an heir, what more do I want?”

sentences.zh: 克寧妻孟氏素剛悍，存顥等各遣其妻入說孟氏，孟氏數以迫克寧。

translations.literal: Kening’s wife Lady Meng was by nature fierce; Cunhao and the others each sent their wives to persuade Lady Meng, and Lady Meng repeatedly pressed Kening.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Meng was fierce; the adoptees’ wives worked on her until she pressed Kening again and again.

sentences.zh: 克寧仁而無斷，惑於群言，遂至於禍。

translations.literal: Kening was benevolent but indecisive, confused by many voices, and came to disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Kening was kind but weak, swayed by many tongues, and fell to ruin.

sentences.zh: 都虞候李存質得罪於克寧，克寧殺之，而與張承業，李存璋有隙，又求兼領大同軍節度使。

translations.literal: The chief adjutant Li Cunzhi had offended Kening and Kening killed him; he had friction with Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang, and also sought to add the military governorship of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He killed adjutant Li Cunzhi for an offense, quarreled with Zhang Chengye and Li Cunzhang, and sought Datong as well.

sentences.zh: 於是幸臣史敬熔見太后，告克寧與存顥謀執王及太后以降梁。

translations.literal: Then the favorite Shi Jingrong saw the empress dowager and reported that Kening and Cunhao plotted to seize the king and dowager and surrender to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Favorite Shi Jingrong told the dowager that Kening and Cunhao meant to seize king and dowager for Liang.

sentences.zh: 莊宗召承業、存璋告之曰：「季父所為如此，奈何？

translations.literal: Zhuangzong summoned Chengye and Cunzhang and said: “My younger uncle has come to this—what can be done?
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong told Chengye and Cunzhang: “My uncle has come to this—what now?

sentences.zh: 然骨肉不可自相魚肉，吾當避賢路以紓禍於吾家。

translations.literal: Yet flesh and blood must not devour each other; I will yield the worthy path to ease calamity for our house.
translations.idiomatic: Yet kin must not devour kin; I will step aside to spare the house.

sentences.zh: 」承業等請誅克寧。

translations.literal: ” Chengye and the others asked to execute Kening.
translations.idiomatic: ” They urged Kening’s death.

sentences.zh: 乃伏兵於府，置酒大會，克寧既至，執而殺之。

translations.literal: They hid troops in the headquarters, set a great feast, and when Kening arrived seized and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Troops lay in wait; at the feast they seized and killed him.

sentences.zh: 太祖七子

translations.literal: Taizu’s seven sons
translations.idiomatic: Taizu’s seven sons

sentences.zh: 太祖子八人：莊宗長子也，次曰存美、存霸、存禮、存渥、存乂、存確、存紀。

translations.literal: Taizu had eight sons: Zhuangzong was the eldest; next Cunmei, Cunba, Cunli, Cunwo, Cunyi, Cunque, and Cunji.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had eight sons: Zhuangzong first, then Cunmei, Cunba, Cunli, Cunwo, Cunyi, Cunque, and Cunji.

sentences.zh: 同光三年十二月辛亥，詔封存美等七人為王。

translations.literal: On xinhai, the twelfth month of the third year of Tongguang, an edict enfeoffed Cunmei and the other seven as princes.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the twelfth month of Tongguang 3, Cunmei and the other seven were made princes.

sentences.zh: 蓋存霸、存渥、存紀與莊宗同母也，存美、存乂、存確、存禮不知其母名氏號位。

translations.literal: Cunba, Cunwo, and Cunji shared a mother with Zhuangzong; Cunmei, Cunyi, Cunque, and Cunli—their mothers’ names and ranks are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Cunba, Cunwo, and Cunji shared Zhuangzong’s mother; the mothers of the others are unknown.

sentences.zh: 存美封邕王，存霸永王，存禮薛王，存渥申王，存乂睦王，存確通王，存紀雅王。

translations.literal: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba Prince of Yong, Cunli Prince of Xue, Cunwo Prince of Shen, Cunyi Prince of Mu, Cunque Prince of Tong, Cunji Prince of Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Cunmei was Prince of Yong, Cunba of Yong (永), Cunli of Xue, Cunwo of Shen, Cunyi of Mu, Cunque of Tong, Cunji of Ya.

sentences.zh: 存乂歷建雄、保大二軍節度使。

translations.literal: Cunyi successively held the Jianxiong and Baoda armies as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Cunyi governed Jianxiong and Baoda.

sentences.zh: 娶郭崇韜女。

translations.literal: He married Guo Chongtao’s daughter.
translations.idiomatic: He married Guo Chongtao’s daughter.

sentences.zh: 是時，魏州妖人楊千郎用事，自言有墨子術，能役使鬼神，化丹砂、水銀。

translations.literal: At that time the Wei sorcerer Yang Qianlang was in favor, claiming Mohist arts to command ghosts and spirits and turn cinnabar and mercury.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei sorcerer Yang Qianlang claimed Mohist arts to command spirits and transmute mercury.

sentences.zh: 莊宗頗神之，拜千郎檢校尚書郎，賜紫，其妻出入宮禁，承恩寵，而士或因之以求官爵，存乂及存渥等往往朋淫於其家。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong treated him as miraculous, made him acting director of the Secretariat with purple robes; his wife entered the forbidden palace and received favor, and gentlemen often used him to seek office; Cunyi and Cunwo often debauched at his house.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong made him acting director with purple robes; his wife entered the palace; Cunyi and Cunwo often caroused there.

sentences.zh: 及崇韜被族，莊宗遣宦官陰察外議以為如何，而宦官因欲盡誅崇韜親黨以絕後患，乃誣言：「存乂過千郎，酒酣，攘臂號泣，為婦翁稱冤，言甚怨望。

translations.literal: When Chongtao’s clan was exterminated Zhuangzong sent eunuchs to probe public opinion; the eunuchs wished to wipe out Chongtao’s kin to cut off future trouble and slandered: “Cunyi visited Qianlang; drunk, he waved his arms and wailed, crying injustice for his father-in-law, words full of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongtao’s clan was killed, eunuchs probed opinion and lied that Cunyi, drunk at Qianlang’s house, had wailed for his father-in-law in rage.

sentences.zh: 」莊宗大怒，以兵圍其第而誅之，並誅千郎。

translations.literal: ” Zhuangzong was furious, surrounded his residence with troops and executed him, and also executed Qianlang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong surrounded his house and killed him and Qianlang.

sentences.zh: 存霸歷昭義、天平、河中三軍節度使，存渥義成、天平二軍節度使，皆居京師，食其俸祿而已。

translations.literal: Cunba held in turn Zhaoyi, Tianping, and Hezhong as military governor; Cunwo held Yicheng and Tianping—both lived in the capital on salary alone.
translations.idiomatic: Cunba held Zhaoyi, Tianping, and Hezhong; Cunwo held Yicheng and Tianping—they lived at court on stipends.

sentences.zh: 趙在禮作亂，乃遣存霸於河中。

translations.literal: When Zhao Zaili rebelled, Cunba was sent to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Zaili rose, Cunba was sent to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源兵反，向京師，莊宗再幸汜水，徙存霸北京留守，存渥河中節度使，宣麻未訖，郭從謙反，攻興教門，存渥從莊宗拒賊。

translations.literal: When Li Siyuan’s troops rebelled toward the capital Zhuangzong again went to Sishui, moved Cunba to northern capital regent and Cunwo to Hezhong military governor; before the decree was finished Guo Congqian rebelled and attacked Xingjiao Gate; Cunwo followed Zhuangzong to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Siyuan marched on the capital, Zhuangzong went to Sishui, made Cunba northern regent and Cunwo governor of Hezhong; before the edict was read Guo Congqian struck; Cunwo fought at his side.

sentences.zh: 莊宗中流矢崩，存渥與劉皇后同奔於太原，行至風谷，為部下所殺。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong was struck by an arrow and died; Cunwo fled with Empress Liu toward Taiyuan; reaching Fenggu his escort killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong fell to an arrow; Cunwo fled with Empress Liu toward Taiyuan and was killed at Fenggu by his own men.

sentences.zh: 存霸聞京師亂，亦自河中奔太原，比至，麾下皆散走，惟使下康從弁不去。

translations.literal: Hearing chaos in the capital, Cunba also fled from Hezhong to Taiyuan; when he arrived his followers scattered; only the servant Kang Congbian did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Cunba fled from Hezhong to Taiyuan; his men scattered; only Kang Congbian stayed.

sentences.zh: 存霸乃剪發、衣僧衣，謁符彥超曰：「願為山僧，冀公庇護。

translations.literal: Cunba then cut his hair, wore monk’s robes, and begged Fu Yanchao: “I wish to be a mountain monk; I beg your protection.
translations.idiomatic: He shaved, donned monk’s robes, and begged Fu Yanchao: “Make me a mountain monk under your protection.

sentences.zh: 」彥超欲留之，為軍眾所殺。

translations.literal: ” Yanchao wished to keep him but the soldiers killed him.
translations.idiomatic: ” Yanchao tried to shelter him; the troops killed him.

sentences.zh: 存紀、存確聞郭從謙反，奔於南山，匿民家。

translations.literal: Cunji and Cunque heard Guo Congqian rebelled and fled to the southern hills, hiding in a commoner’s house.
translations.idiomatic: Cunji and Cunque fled to the southern hills and hid with peasants.

sentences.zh: 明宗詔河南府及諸道：「諸王出奔，所至送赴闕；

translations.literal: Mingzong decreed to Henan and all circuits: “Princes who flee are to be sent to court wherever found;
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong ordered the provinces: “Fugitive princes are to be sent to court;

sentences.zh: 如不幸物故者，收瘞以聞。

translations.literal: if they die by misfortune, bury them and report.
translations.idiomatic: if they die, bury them and report.”

sentences.zh: 」存紀等所匿民家以告安重誨，重誨謂霍彥威曰：「二王逃難，主上尋求，恐其所失。

translations.literal: The house where Cunji and Cunque hid reported to An Chonghui; Chonghui said to Huo Yanwei: “The two princes fled in hardship; the throne seeks them—what if they are lost?
translations.idiomatic: Their hosts informed An Chonghui, who told Huo Yanwei: “The throne seeks them—what if they are lost?

sentences.zh: 今上既監國典喪，此禮如何？

translations.literal: The emperor now oversees the funeral rites—how is this ritual?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor now rules the mourning—what rite fits?

sentences.zh: 」彥威曰：「上性仁慈，不可聞奏。

translations.literal: Yanwei said: “His Majesty is by nature benevolent—this must not be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwei said: “He is merciful—do not report it.

sentences.zh: 宜密為之所，以安人情。

translations.literal: Better act secretly to settle people’s hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Act in secret to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 」乃即民家殺之。

translations.literal: They went at once to the house and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: They went to the house and killed them.

sentences.zh: 存美素病風，居太原，與存禮皆不知其所終。

translations.literal: Cunmei had long been ill with wind and lived at Taiyuan; with Cunli their ends are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Cunmei, ill with palsy, lived at Taiyuan; he and Cunli vanished from the record.

sentences.zh: ○莊宗五子

translations.literal: ○ Zhuangzong’s five sons
translations.idiomatic: ○ Zhuangzong’s five sons

sentences.zh: 莊宗五子、長曰繼岌，其次繼潼、繼嵩、繼蟾、繼峣。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong’s five sons: the eldest Jiji, then Jitong, Jisong, Jichan, and Jiyao.
translations.idiomatic: Five sons: Jiji first, then Jitong, Jisong, Jichan, and Jiyao.

sentences.zh: 繼岌母曰劉皇后，其四皆不著其母名號。

translations.literal: Jiji’s mother was Empress Liu; the other four— their mothers’ names are not given.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji’s mother was Empress Liu; the other mothers are unnamed.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位，繼岌為北都留守，判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne Jiji was northern capital regent and judged the Six Armies and guards.
translations.idiomatic: At his accession Jiji was northern regent over the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He became acting Grand Preceptor and co-equal with the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 豆盧革為相，建言：唐故事，皇子皆為宮使。

translations.literal: Doulu Ge as chief minister proposed: by Tang precedent princes all held palace commands.
translations.idiomatic: Doulu Ge said Tang custom made princes palace commissioners.

sentences.zh: 因以鄴宮為興聖宮，以繼岌為使。

translations.literal: Thus the Ye palace became Xingsheng Palace and Jiji was made its commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The Ye palace became Xingsheng and Jiji its commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，封魏王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang he was enfeoffed Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 he was made Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 是歲伐蜀，以繼岌為西南面行營都統，郭崇韜為都招討使，工部尚書任圜、翰林學士李愚皆參軍事。

translations.literal: That year they attacked Shu; Jiji was overall commander of the southwestern campaign, Guo Chongtao grand marshal, the Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu both staff officers.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Shu campaign made Jiji supreme commander, Guo Chongtao grand marshal, Ren Yuan and Li Yu on staff.

sentences.zh: 九月戊申，將兵六萬自鳳翔入大散關，軍無十日之糧，而所至州鎮皆迎降，遂食其粟。

translations.literal: On wushen, the ninth month, he led sixty thousand from Fengxiang through Dasan Pass; the army had only ten days’ grain, yet every prefecture and garrison submitted and they ate local stores.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen in the ninth month sixty thousand marched from Fengxiang through Dasan with ten days’ grain; every town submitted and fed them.

sentences.zh: 至興州，蜀將程奉璉以五百騎降，因以其兵修閣道，以過唐軍。

translations.literal: Reaching Xingzhou, the Shu general Cheng Fenglian surrendered with five hundred horse; they used his men to repair the road for the Tang army.
translations.idiomatic: At Xing, Cheng Fenglian surrendered with five hundred horse and repaired the road.

sentences.zh: 王衍將兵萬人屯利州，分其半逆戰於三泉，為先鋒康延孝所敗，衍懼，斷吉柏江浮橋，奔歸成都。

translations.literal: Wang Yan led ten thousand at Lizhou and sent half to meet the Tang at Sanquan; the vanguard Kang Yanxiao defeated them; Yan feared, cut the Jibo floating bridge, and fled to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan held Lizhou with ten thousand; half met Tang at Sanquan and lost to Kang Yanxiao; Yan cut the Jibo bridge and fled to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 唐軍自文州間道以入。

translations.literal: The Tang army entered by a path from Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tang entered by a path from Wen.

sentences.zh: 十月己酉，繼岌至綿州，衍上箋請降。

translations.literal: On jiyou, the tenth month, Jiji reached Mianzhou; Yan submitted a letter asking to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the tenth month Jiji reached Mian; Yan asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，入成都。

translations.literal: On bingchen they entered Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen they entered Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 王衍乘竹輿至升仙橋，素衣、牽羊，草索系首，肉袒、銜璧、輿櫬，群臣衰绖，徒跣以降。

translations.literal: Wang Yan rode a bamboo litter to Ascension Bridge in plain clothes, leading a sheep, grass rope on his neck, bare chest with jade tablet in his mouth, coffin on a cart; ministers in mourning hemp, barefoot, came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan came in plain clothes on a bamboo litter, leading a sheep, rope on his neck, jade in his mouth, coffin on a cart; ministers barefoot in hemp followed.

sentences.zh: 繼岌下而取璧，崇韜解縛，焚櫬。

translations.literal: Jiji descended and took the tablet; Chongtao undid the bonds and burned the coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji took the tablet; Chongtao cut the bonds and burned the coffin.

sentences.zh: 自出師至降衍，凡七十五日，兵不血刃，自古用兵之易，未有如此。

translations.literal: From the march to Yan’s surrender, seventy-five days; not a blade bloodied—never in antiquity was campaigning so easy.
translations.idiomatic: Seventy-five days from march to surrender without a bloody blade—war had never been so easy.

sentences.zh: 然繼岌雖為都統，而軍政號令一出崇韜。

translations.literal: Yet though Jiji was overall commander, military orders all came from Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: Though Jiji commanded, every order came from Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 初，莊宗遣宦者供奉官李從襲監中軍，高品李廷安、呂知柔為典謁。

translations.literal: At first Zhuangzong had sent the eunuch attendant Li Congxi to oversee the central army, and the senior eunuchs Li Ting’an and Lü Zhirou as ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong had sent Li Congxi to oversee the center and Li Ting’an and Lü Zhirou as ushers.

sentences.zh: 從襲等素惡崇韜，又見崇韜專任軍事，益不平之。

translations.literal: Congxi and the others had long hated Chongtao and, seeing him monopolize military affairs, were even more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: They hated Chongtao and resented his monopoly of command.

sentences.zh: 及破蜀，蜀之貴臣大將，自王宗弼已下，皆爭以蜀寶貨，妓樂奉崇韜父子，而魏王所得，匹馬、束帛、唾壺、麈柄而已；

translations.literal: Chongtao daily decided military affairs; generals, clerks, and guests hurried filling the court, while at the overall command only great generals paid morning calls—the牙 gate was silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao’s hall thronged with officers and guests while the prince’s gate stood empty but for morning calls.

sentences.zh: 崇韜日決軍事，將吏賓客趨走盈庭，而都統府惟大將晨謁，牙門闐然。

translations.literal: From this Congxi and the others could not contain their rage.
translations.idiomatic: Congxi and the others boiled with resentment.

sentences.zh: 由是從襲等不勝其憤。

translations.literal: Soon Zongbi led Shu people to see Jiji and asked to leave Chongtao to garrison Shu; Congxi and the others then said Chongtao had a different intent and urged Jiji to guard against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zongbi asked Jiji to leave Chongtao in Shu; Congxi claimed treason and urged caution.

sentences.zh: 已而宗弼率蜀人見繼岌，請留崇韜鎮蜀，從襲等因言崇韜有異志，勸繼岌為備。

translations.literal: Jiji told Chongtao: “His Majesty relies on you as on Yi Yin and Huo Guang, honors you above the temple, expecting you to pacify all under Heaven and master the four barbarians—surely he will not abandon an elder in barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji told Chongtao: “Father trusts you as Yi Yin and Huo Guang—he will not leave you in the wilds.

sentences.zh: 繼岌謂崇韜曰：「陛下倚侍中如衡、華，尊之廟堂之上，期以一天下而制四夷，必不棄元老於蠻夷之地。

translations.literal: This matter is not what I dare to know.”
translations.idiomatic: That is not for me to say.”

sentences.zh: 此事非予敢知也。」

translations.literal: Zhuangzong heard Chongtao wished to remain in Shu and was also displeased; he sent the eunuch Xiang Yansi to urge Jiji to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Chongtao might stay, Zhuangzong sent Xiang Yansi to hurry withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 莊宗聞崇韜欲留蜀，亦不悅，遣宦者向延嗣趣繼岌班師。

translations.literal: Yansi reached Chengdu; Chongtao did not come out to meet him; when they met his courtesy grew even colder; Yansi was angry, and Congxi and the others reported Chongtao had a different intent and might endanger the Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu Chongtao snubbed Yansi; Congxi accused him of plotting against the prince.

sentences.zh: 延嗣至成都，崇韜不出迎，及見，禮益慢，延嗣怒，從襲等因告延嗣崇韜有異志，恐危魏王。

translations.literal: Yansi returned and reported it all.
translations.idiomatic: Yansi returned and told all.

sentences.zh: 延嗣還，具言之。

translations.literal: Empress Liu wept and begged to preserve Jiji; Zhuangzong sent the eunuch Ma Yan’gui to see whether Chongtao would leave.
translations.idiomatic: The empress wept for Jiji; Zhuangzong sent Ma Yan’gui to watch Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 劉皇后涕泣請保全繼岌，莊宗遣宦官馬彥珪往視崇韜去就。

translations.literal: The two Sichuans were newly pacified; Meng Zhixiang had not yet arrived; bandits still gathered in the hills; Chongtao was sending Ren Yuan and others to recruit them, fearing trouble later, so the army did not return at once.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was new; bandits roamed; Chongtao delayed withdrawal while Ren Yuan pacified the hills.

sentences.zh: 是時，兩川新定，孟知祥未至，所在盜賊聚山林，崇韜方遣任圜等分出招集，恐後生變，故師未即還。

translations.literal: As Yan’gui was about to go he saw Empress Liu: “I heard from Yansi that affairs in Shu are already beyond remedy; disaster will strike in an instant—how can one go three thousand li back and forth for orders from the granary!
translations.idiomatic: Yan’gui told the empress: “Shu is lost—disaster is instant—no time for orders from home!

sentences.zh: 而彥珪將行，見劉皇后曰：「臣見延嗣言蜀中事勢已不可，禍機之作，間不容發，安能三千里往復廩命乎！

translations.literal: ” The empress told Zhuangzong Liu’s words; Zhuangzong said: “Rumor is unverified—how can we decide at once?
translations.idiomatic: ” She told Zhuangzong; he said: “Rumors are not proof.

sentences.zh: 」劉皇后以彥珪語告莊宗，莊宗曰：「傳言未審，豈可便令果決？

translations.literal: ” The empress could not obtain permission and herself wrote a command to Jiji to kill Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: ” She wrote her own order to Jiji to kill Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 」皇后不得請，因自為教與繼岌，使殺崇韜。

translations.literal: ” The empress could not obtain permission and herself wrote a command to Jiji to kill Chongtao.
translations.idiomatic: ” She wrote her own order to Jiji to kill Chongtao.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，崇韜留任圜守蜀，以待知祥之至，崇韜期班師有日。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year Chongtao left Ren Yuan to hold Shu until Zhixiang arrived; Chongtao set a day to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Next first month Chongtao left Ren Yuan in Shu and prepared to march.

sentences.zh: 彥珪至蜀，出皇后教示繼岌，繼岌曰：「今大軍將發，未有釁端，豈可作此負心事！

translations.literal: Yan’gui reached Shu and showed the empress’s command to Jiji; Jiji said: “The great army is about to march; there is no sign of trouble—how can we do this shameful deed!
translations.idiomatic: Yan’gui showed the order; Jiji said: “We are marching—how can we murder our marshal!

sentences.zh: 」從襲等泣曰：「今有密敕，王茍不行，使崇韜知之，則吾屬無類矣！

translations.literal: ” Congxi and the others wept: “Now there is a secret decree—if the prince will not act and Chongtao learns of it, none of us will survive!
translations.idiomatic: ” Congxi wept: “Disobey and we are all dead when he learns of it!

sentences.zh: 」繼岌曰：「上無詔書，徒以皇后手教，安能殺招討使？

translations.literal: ” Jiji said: “There is no edict from above—only the empress’s hand command—how can we kill the grand marshal?
translations.idiomatic: ” Jiji said: “There is no imperial edict—only her note.

sentences.zh: 」從襲等力爭，繼岌不得已而從之。

translations.literal: ” Congxi and the others argued fiercely; Jiji had no choice but to agree.
translations.idiomatic: ” They pressed him until he yielded.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，從襲以都統命召崇韜，繼岌登樓以避之。

translations.literal: At dawn Congxi, by overall command order, summoned Chongtao; Jiji mounted the tower to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Congxi summoned Chongtao; Jiji hid on the tower.

sentences.zh: 崇韜入，升階，繼岌從者李環撾碎其首。

translations.literal: Chongtao entered and ascended the steps; Jiji’s follower Li Huan smashed his skull.
translations.idiomatic: Chongtao entered; Li Huan shattered his skull.

sentences.zh: 繼岌遂班師。

translations.literal: Jiji then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji marched home.

sentences.zh: 二月，軍至泥溪，先鋒康延孝叛，據漢州，繼岌遣任圜討平之。

translations.literal: In the second month the army reached Nixi; the vanguard Kang Yanxiao rebelled and held Hanzhou; Jiji sent Ren Yuan to pacify him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month at Nixi, Kang Yanxiao rebelled at Han; Ren Yuan crushed him.

sentences.zh: 四月辛卯，至興平，聞明宗反，兵入京師，繼岌欲退保鳳翔。

translations.literal: On xinmao, the fourth month, they reached Xingping; hearing Mingzong had rebelled and troops entered the capital, Jiji wished to fall back on Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in the fourth month at Xingping, hearing Mingzong had taken the capital, Jiji meant to hold Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 至武功，李從襲勸繼岌馳趨京師，以救內難。

translations.literal: Reaching Wugong, Li Congxi urged Jiji to gallop to the capital to save the inner crisis.
translations.idiomatic: At Wugong, Li Congxi urged a dash to save the throne.

sentences.zh: 行至渭河，西都留守張抃斷浮橋，繼岌不得度，乃循河而東，至渭南，左右皆潰。

translations.literal: Reaching the Wei River, the western capital regent Zhang Bian cut the floating bridge; Jiji could not cross and went east along the river to Weinan; his attendants all fled.
translations.idiomatic: At the Wei, Zhang Bian cut the bridge; blocked, Jiji went east to Weinan as his guard melted away.

sentences.zh: 從襲謂繼岌曰：「大事已去，福不可再，王宜自圖。

translations.literal: Congxi told Jiji: “The great affair is lost; fortune will not come twice—you should plan for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Congxi said: “All is lost—save yourself.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌徘徊泣下，謂李環曰：「吾道盡途窮，子當殺我。

translations.literal: Jiji lingered, weeping, and told Li Huan: “My road is ended— you should kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji wept to Li Huan: “End it for me.

sentences.zh: 」環遲疑久之，謂繼岌乳母曰：「吾不忍見王，王若無路求生，當踣面以俟。

translations.literal: Huan hesitated long and told Jiji’s wet nurse: “I cannot bear to see the prince—if he has no way to live, let him fall face down and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Huan told the nurse: “I cannot watch—if there is no way, let him lie face down.

sentences.zh: 」繼岌面榻而臥，環縊殺之。

translations.literal: Jiji lay face down on the couch; Huan strangled him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji lay on the couch; Huan strangled him.

sentences.zh: 任圜從後至，葬繼岌華州之西南。

translations.literal: Ren Yuan came after and buried Jiji southwest of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Yuan came after and buried him southwest of Hua.

sentences.zh: 繼岌少病閹，無子。

translations.literal: Jiji from youth suffered eunuchism and had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Jiji had been castrated young and left no sons.

sentences.zh: 明宗已即位，圜率征蜀之師二萬至京師，明宗撫慰久之，問圜繼岌何在，圜具言繼岌死狀。

translations.literal: Mingzong had already taken the throne; Yuan led the Shu expedition’s twenty thousand to the capital; Mingzong comforted them long and asked Yuan where Jiji was; Yuan told fully how Jiji died.
translations.idiomatic: Mingzong welcomed Ren Yuan’s twenty thousand from Shu and asked for Jiji; Yuan told how he died.

sentences.zh: 同光三年，詔以皇子繼嵩、繼潼、繼蟾、繼峣皆為光祿大夫，檢校司徒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tongguang an edict made the princes Jisong, Jitong, Jichan, and Jiyao all Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness, acting secretaries.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 3 Jisong, Jitong, Jichan, and Jiyao were made Grand Masters and acting secretaries.

sentences.zh: 蓋其皆幼，故不封。

translations.literal: They were all young, so they were not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: They were too young to be enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 當莊宗遇弒時，太祖子孫在者十有一人，明宗入立，其四人見殺，其餘皆不知所終，太祖之後遂絕。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong was assassinated eleven of Taizu’s descendants still lived; when Mingzong took the throne four were killed and the rest vanished—Taizu’s line was extinct.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhuangzong’s death eleven of Taizu’s line still lived; Mingzong killed four and the rest disappeared—Taizu’s house was ended.
